entries.title: Two Sum
entries.problemStatement:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.

You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

You can return the answer in any order.
entries.description: Find two numbers in an array that add up to a target value
entries.fuzzyStatement: Given an array of numbers, find two that add up to a target value.

examples.explanation: Because nums[0] + nums[1] == 9, we return [0, 1].

entries.title: Contains Duplicate
entries.problemStatement: Given an integer array nums, return true if any value appears at least twice in the array, and return false if every element is distinct.
entries.description: Determine if an array contains any duplicates

entries.title: Product of Array Except Self
entries.problemStatement:
Given an integer array nums, return an array answer such that answer[i] is equal to the product of all the elements of nums except nums[i].

The product of any prefix or suffix of nums is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit integer.

You must write an algorithm that runs in O(n) time and without using the division operation.
entries.description: Calculate product of all elements except current element
constraints: The product of any prefix or suffix of nums is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit integer

entries.title: Group Anagrams
entries.problemStatement:
Given an array of strings strs, group the anagrams together. You can return the answer in any order.

An Anagram is a word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of a different word or phrase, typically using all the original letters exactly once.
entries.description: Group strings that are anagrams of each other
constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters

entries.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
entries.problemStatement:
Given an unsorted array of integers nums, return the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence.

You must write an algorithm that runs in O(n) time.
entries.description: Find the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence

examples.explanation: The longest consecutive elements sequence is [1, 2, 3, 4]. Therefore its length is 4.

entries.title: First Missing Positive
entries.problemStatement: Given an unsorted integer array nums, return the smallest missing positive integer. Must run in O(n) time and use O(1) auxiliary space.
entries.description: Find smallest missing positive integer in O(n) time and O(1) space.

entries.title: Valid Anagram
entries.problemStatement:
Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s, and false otherwise.

An Anagram is a word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of a different word or phrase, typically using all the original letters exactly once.
entries.description: Determine if two strings are anagrams of each other
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters

entries.title: Top K Frequent Elements
entries.problemStatement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements. You may return the answer in any order.
entries.description: Find k most frequent elements in an array
constraints: k is in the range [1, the number of unique elements]
The answer is guaranteed to be unique

entries.title: Encode and Decode Strings
entries.problemStatement:
Design an algorithm to encode a list of strings to a single string. The encoded string is then decoded back to the original list of strings.

Implement encode and decode functions.
entries.description: Design an algorithm to encode and decode a list of strings

examples.explanation: Encode to a single string, then decode back to original list

constraints: strs[i] contains any possible characters out of 256 valid ASCII characters

entries.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
entries.problemStatement:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer k, return the total number of subarrays whose sum equals to k.

A subarray is a contiguous non-empty sequence of elements within an array.
entries.description: Count subarrays with sum equal to k using prefix sum

examples.explanation: Subarrays [1,1] at index 0-1 and 1-2
Subarrays [1,2] and [3]

entries.title: Find All Duplicates in an Array
entries.problemStatement:
Given an integer array nums of length n where all the integers of nums are in the range [1, n] and each integer appears once or twice, return an array of all the integers that appear twice.

You must write an algorithm that runs in O(n) time and uses only constant extra space.
entries.description: Find all duplicates in O(n) time and O(1) extra space
constraints: Each element in nums appears once or twice

entries.title: Next Permutation
entries.problemStatement:
A permutation of an array of integers is an arrangement of its members into a sequence or linear order.

The next permutation of an array of integers is the next lexicographically greater permutation of its integer. If such arrangement is not possible, the array must be rearranged as the lowest possible order (i.e., sorted in ascending order).

For example:
- For arr = [1,2,3], the next permutation is [1,3,2].
- For arr = [3,2,1], the next permutation is [1,2,3] (no greater permutation exists).
- For arr = [1,1,5], the next permutation is [1,5,1].

The replacement must be in place and use only constant extra memory.
entries.description: Find the next lexicographically greater permutation of numbers

entries.title: Majority Element
entries.problemStatement:
Given an array nums of size n, return the majority element.

The majority element is the element that appears more than ⌊n / 2⌋ times. You may assume that the majority element always exists in the array.

Follow-up: Could you solve the problem in linear time and in O(1) space?
entries.description: Find the element that appears more than n/2 times using Boyer-Moore algorithm

entries.title: Rotate Array
entries.problemStatement:
Given an integer array nums, rotate the array to the right by k steps, where k is non-negative.

Follow up:
- Try to come up with as many solutions as you can. There are at least three different ways to solve this problem.
- Could you do it in-place with O(1) extra space?
entries.description: Rotate an array to the right by k steps in-place

entries.title: 3Sum
entries.problemStatement:
Given an integer array nums, return all the triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that i != j, i != k, and j != k, and nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0.

Notice that the solution set must not contain duplicate triplets.
entries.description: Find all unique triplets that sum to zero
entries.fuzzyStatement: Given an array of numbers, find all unique triplets that sum to zero.

entries.title: Trapping Rain Water (Two Pointers)
entries.problemStatement: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
entries.description: Calculate how much water can be trapped after raining given an elevation map

examples.explanation: The elevation map traps 6 units of rain water.

entries.title: Container With Most Water
entries.problemStatement:
Given n non-negative integers a1, a2, ..., an, where each represents a point at coordinate (i, ai). n vertical lines are drawn such that the two endpoints of the line i is at (i, ai) and (i, 0). Find two lines, which, together with the x-axis forms a container, such that the container contains the most water.

Notice that you may not slant the container.
entries.description: Find two lines that together with the x-axis form a container that holds the most water.

examples.explanation: The maximum area is between index 1 and 8 (height 8 and 7), area = min(8,7) * (8-1) = 7 * 7 = 49

entries.title: Longest Palindromic Substring
entries.problemStatement:
Given a string s, return the longest palindromic substring in s.

A palindromic string reads the same backward as forward.
entries.description: Find the longest palindromic substring in a string.

examples.explanation: "aba" is also a valid answer

constraints: s consist of only digits and English letters

entries.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
entries.problemStatement:
Given an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order, remove the duplicates in-place such that each unique element appears only once. The relative order of the elements should be kept the same. Then return the number of unique elements in nums.

Consider the number of unique elements of nums to be k. To get accepted, you need to:
- Change the array nums such that the first k elements contain the unique elements in the order they were present originally.
- Return k.
entries.description: Remove duplicates in-place from sorted array

examples.explanation: Function returns k = 2, with first two elements being 1 and 2.
Function returns k = 5.

constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order

entries.title: Move Zeroes
entries.problemStatement:
Given an integer array nums, move all 0's to the end of it while maintaining the relative order of the non-zero elements.

Note that you must do this in-place without making a copy of the array.
entries.description: Move all zeroes to end while maintaining order

entries.title: Valid Palindrome
entries.problemStatement:
A phrase is a palindrome if, after converting all uppercase letters into lowercase letters and removing all non-alphanumeric characters, it reads the same forward and backward. Alphanumeric characters include letters and numbers.

Given a string s, return true if it is a palindrome, or false otherwise.
entries.description: Check if string is palindrome ignoring non-alphanumeric

examples.input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"
examples.explanation: "amanaplanacanalpanama" is a palindrome.
"raceacar" is not a palindrome.
After removing non-alphanumeric characters, it's empty, which is a palindrome.

constraints: s consists only of printable ASCII characters

entries.title: Sort Colors
entries.problemStatement:
Given an array nums with n objects colored red, white, or blue, sort them in-place so that objects of the same color are adjacent, with the colors in the order red, white, and blue.

We will use the integers 0, 1, and 2 to represent the color red, white, and blue, respectively.

You must solve this problem without using the library's sort function.

Follow up: Could you come up with a one-pass algorithm using only constant extra space?
entries.description: Sort array with only 0, 1, 2 in one pass (Dutch National Flag)

entries.title: Reverse String
entries.problemStatement:
Write a function that reverses a string. The input string is given as an array of characters s.

You must do this by modifying the input array in-place with O(1) extra memory.
entries.description: Reverse a string array in-place
constraints: s[i] is a printable ascii character

entries.title: Partition Labels
entries.problemStatement:
You are given a string s. We want to partition the string into as many parts as possible so that each letter appears in at most one part.

Note that the partition is done so that after concatenating all the parts in order, the resultant string should be s.

Return a list of integers representing the size of these parts.
entries.description: Partition string into parts where each letter appears in one part only

examples.explanation: The partition is "ababcbaca", "defegde", "hijhklij". Each letter appears in at most one part.
All letters are interconnected, so single partition.

constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters

entries.title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
entries.problemStatement:
Given a 1-indexed array of integers numbers that is already sorted in non-decreasing order, find two numbers such that they add up to a specific target number. Let these two numbers be numbers[index1] and numbers[index2] where 1 <= index1 < index2 <= numbers.length.

Return the indices of the two numbers, index1 and index2, added by one as an integer array [index1, index2] of length 2.

The tests are generated such that there is exactly one solution. You may not use the same element twice.

Your solution must use only constant extra space.
entries.description: Find two numbers in sorted array that add up to target

examples.explanation: The sum of 2 and 7 is 9. Therefore, index1 = 1, index2 = 2.

constraints: numbers is sorted in non-decreasing order
The tests are generated such that there is exactly one solution

entries.title: 4Sum
entries.problemStatement:
Given an array nums of n integers, return an array of all the unique quadruplets [nums[a], nums[b], nums[c], nums[d]] such that:

- 0 <= a, b, c, d < n
- a, b, c, d are distinct
- nums[a] + nums[b] + nums[c] + nums[d] == target

You may return the answer in any order.
entries.description: Find all unique quadruplets that sum to target

entries.title: Squares of a Sorted Array
entries.problemStatement: Given an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order, return an array of the squares of each number sorted in non-decreasing order.
entries.description: Return squares of sorted array in sorted order

examples.explanation: After squaring: [16,1,0,9,100]. After sorting: [0,1,9,16,100].

constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order

entries.title: Boats to Save People
entries.problemStatement:
You are given an array people where people[i] is the weight of the ith person, and an infinite number of boats where each boat can carry a maximum weight of limit. Each boat carries at most two people at the same time, provided the sum of the weight of those people is at most limit.

Return the minimum number of boats to carry every given person.
entries.description: Find minimum boats to carry all people with weight limit

examples.explanation: 1 boat (1, 2)

entries.title: Merge Sorted Array
entries.problemStatement:
You are given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2, sorted in non-decreasing order, and two integers m and n, representing the number of elements in nums1 and nums2 respectively.

Merge nums1 and nums2 into a single array sorted in non-decreasing order.

The final sorted array should not be returned by the function, but instead be stored inside the array nums1. To accommodate this, nums1 has a length of m + n, where the first m elements denote the elements that should be merged, and the last n elements are set to 0 and should be ignored. nums2 has a length of n.
entries.description: Merge two sorted arrays into one sorted array in-place
entries.fuzzyStatement: Merge two sorted arrays into one sorted array.

examples.explanation: The arrays we are merging are [1,2,3] and [2,5,6]. The result is [1,2,2,3,5,6].
The arrays we are merging are [1] and []. The result is [1].
The arrays we are merging are [] and [1]. The result is [1].

entries.title: Difference Between Sums at Even and Odd Indices
entries.problemStatement:
Given an integer array nums, calculate the sum of elements at even indices and the sum of elements at odd indices. Return the difference (even sum - odd sum).

Only consider elements within the range [-100, 100]. Elements outside this range should be ignored.
entries.description: Calculate the difference between sums of elements at even and odd indices
entries.fuzzyStatement: Given an array, find the difference between sums at even and odd positions.

examples.explanation: Even indices (0, 2, 4): 1 + 3 + 5 = 9. Odd indices (1, 3): 2 + 4 = 6. Difference: 9 - 6 = 3.
Even indices: 10 + 30 = 40. Odd indices: 20 + 40 = 60. Difference: 40 - 60 = -20.
200 is outside [-100, 100] so ignored. Even: 5 + 10 = 15. Odd: -5 = -5. Difference: 15 - (-5) = 20.

entries.title: Student with Highest Average Score
entries.problemStatement:
You are given a list of student score records. Each record contains a student name and a score. A student may have multiple scores.

Calculate the average score for each student and return the name of the student with the highest average. If there's a tie, return the name that comes first alphabetically.
entries.description: Find the student with the highest average score from a list of records
entries.fuzzyStatement: Given a list of student scores, find who has the highest average.

examples.explanation: Alice's average: (90 + 95) / 2 = 92.5. Bob's average: (85 + 80) / 2 = 82.5. Alice wins.
Both have average 100. Charlie comes first alphabetically.

entries.title: Valid Parentheses
entries.problemStatement:
Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid.

An input string is valid if:
1. Open brackets must be closed by the same type of brackets.
2. Open brackets must be closed in the correct order.
3. Every close bracket has a corresponding open bracket of the same type.
entries.description: Determine if a string containing parentheses is valid
entries.fuzzyStatement: Given a string of brackets, determine if it's valid.

entries.title: Min Stack
entries.problemStatement:
Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element in constant time.

Implement the MinStack class:
- MinStack() initializes the stack object.
- void push(int val) pushes the element val onto the stack.
- void pop() removes the element on the top of the stack.
- int top() gets the top element of the stack.
- int getMin() retrieves the minimum element in the stack.

You must implement a solution with O(1) time complexity for each function.
entries.description: Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element in constant time

examples.input: MinStack(); push(-2); push(0); push(-3); getMin(); pop(); top(); getMin()
examples.explanation: getMin() returns -3. After pop, top is 0 and min is -2.

constraints: Methods pop, top and getMin will always be called on non-empty stacks
At most 3 * 10^4 calls will be made to push, pop, top, and getMin

entries.title: Daily Temperatures
entries.problemStatement: Given an array of integers temperatures represents the daily temperatures, return an array answer such that answer[i] is the number of days you have to wait after the ith day to get a warmer temperature. If there is no future day for which this is possible, keep answer[i] == 0 instead.
entries.description: Find days until warmer temperature using monotonic stack

examples.explanation: For day 0 (73°), the next warmer is day 1 (74°), so answer[0] = 1.

entries.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
entries.problemStatement: Given an array of integers heights representing the histogram's bar height where the width of each bar is 1, return the area of the largest rectangle in the histogram.
entries.description: Find the largest rectangular area in a histogram

examples.explanation: The largest rectangle has area = 10 (bars at index 2 and 3 with height 5).

entries.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
entries.problemStatement:
You are given an array of strings tokens that represents an arithmetic expression in a Reverse Polish Notation.

Evaluate the expression. Return an integer that represents the value of the expression.

Note that:
- The valid operators are '+', '-', '*', and '/'.
- Each operand may be an integer or another expression.
- The division between two integers always truncates toward zero.
- There will not be any division by zero.
- The input represents a valid arithmetic expression in reverse polish notation.
entries.description: Evaluate arithmetic expression in Reverse Polish Notation
constraints: tokens[i] is either an operator or an integer in range [-200, 200]

entries.title: Decode String
entries.problemStatement:
Given an encoded string, return its decoded string.

The encoding rule is: k[encoded_string], where the encoded_string inside the square brackets is being repeated exactly k times. Note that k is guaranteed to be a positive integer.

You may assume that the input string is always valid; there are no extra white spaces, square brackets are well-formed, etc. Furthermore, you may assume that the original data does not contain any digits and that digits are only for those repeat numbers, k.
entries.description: Decode an encoded string with nested patterns

examples.explanation: Inner 2[c] = "cc", then 3[acc] = "accaccacc"

constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters, digits, and square brackets
s is guaranteed to be a valid input
All the integers in s are in the range [1, 300]

entries.title: Asteroid Collision
entries.problemStatement:
We are given an array asteroids of integers representing asteroids in a row.

For each asteroid, the absolute value represents its size, and the sign represents its direction (positive meaning right, negative meaning left). Each asteroid moves at the same speed.

Find out the state of the asteroids after all collisions. If two asteroids meet, the smaller one will explode. If both are the same size, both will explode. Two asteroids moving in the same direction will never meet.
entries.description: Simulate asteroid collisions using a stack

examples.explanation: The 10 and -5 collide resulting in 10. The 5 and 10 never collide.
The 8 and -8 collide exploding each other.
The 2 and -5 collide resulting in -5. The 10 and -5 collide resulting in 10.

entries.title: Simplify Path
entries.problemStatement:
Given a string path, which is an absolute path (starting with a slash '/') to a file or directory in a Unix-style file system, convert it to the simplified canonical path.

In a Unix-style file system, a period '.' refers to the current directory, a double period '..' refers to the directory up a level, and any multiple consecutive slashes are treated as a single slash '/'. The canonical path should:
- Start with a single slash '/'
- Not end with a trailing '/'
- Only contain the directories on the path from the root directory to the target file or directory
entries.description: Simplify Unix-style file path using a stack

examples.explanation: Remove trailing slash.
Going up from root stays at root.
Multiple slashes are replaced by single slash.

constraints: path consists of English letters, digits, period, slash, or underscore
path is a valid absolute Unix path

entries.title: Basic Calculator
entries.problemStatement:
Given a string s representing a valid expression, implement a basic calculator to evaluate it, and return the result of the evaluation.

Note: You are not allowed to use any built-in function which evaluates strings as mathematical expressions.

The expression string may contain:
- '+' and '-' operators
- '(' and ')' parentheses
- ' ' spaces
- Non-negative integers
entries.description: Implement a basic calculator with parentheses

entries.title: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates In String II
entries.problemStatement:
You are given a string s and an integer k, a k duplicate removal consists of choosing k adjacent and equal letters from s and removing them, causing the left and the right side of the deleted substring to concatenate together.

We repeatedly make k duplicate removals on s until we no longer can.

Return the final string after all such duplicate removals have been made. It is guaranteed that the answer is unique.
entries.description: Remove k adjacent duplicate letters using a stack

examples.explanation: No adjacent duplicates.
"eee" -> "ddbcccbdaa" -> "ddbbbdaa" -> "dddaa" -> "aa"

constraints: s only contains lowercase English letters

entries.title: Longest Valid Parentheses
entries.problemStatement: Given a string containing just the characters '(' and ')', return the length of the longest valid (well-formed) parentheses substring.
entries.description: Find the length of the longest valid parentheses substring

examples.explanation: The longest valid parentheses substring is "()".
The longest valid parentheses substring is "()()".

entries.title: Car Fleet
entries.problemStatement:
There are n cars going to the same destination along a one-lane road. The destination is target miles away.

You are given two integer arrays position and speed, both of length n, where position[i] is the position of the ith car and speed[i] is the speed of the ith car (in miles per hour).

A car can never pass another car ahead of it, but it can catch up to it and drive bumper to bumper at the same speed. The faster car will slow down to match the slower car's speed. A car fleet is some non-empty set of cars driving at the same position and same speed.

Return the number of car fleets that will arrive at the destination.
entries.description: Calculate number of car fleets that arrive at destination

examples.explanation: Car at 10 forms fleet 1. Cars at 8,5,3 catch up to car at 10 forming fleet 2. Car at 0 is fleet 3.

entries.title: Trapping Rain Water
entries.problemStatement: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
entries.description: Calculate how much water can be trapped after rain

examples.explanation: The elevation map traps 6 units of rain water.

entries.title: Next Greater Element I
entries.problemStatement:
The next greater element of some element x in an array is the first greater element that is to the right of x in the same array.

You are given two distinct 0-indexed integer arrays nums1 and nums2, where nums1 is a subset of nums2.

For each 0 <= i < nums1.length, find the index j such that nums1[i] == nums2[j] and determine the next greater element of nums2[j] in nums2. If there is no next greater element, then the answer for this query is -1.

Return an array ans of length nums1.length such that ans[i] is the next greater element as described above.
entries.description: Find the next greater element for each element from a subset

examples.explanation: For 4: no greater to right. For 1: 3 is next greater. For 2: no greater.

constraints: All integers in nums1 and nums2 are unique.

entries.title: Next Greater Element II
entries.problemStatement:
Given a circular integer array nums (i.e., the next element of nums[nums.length - 1] is nums[0]), return the next greater number for every element in nums.

The next greater number of a number x is the first greater number to its traversing-order next in the array, which means you could search circularly to find its next greater number. If it doesn't exist, return -1 for this number.
entries.description: Find next greater element in a circular array

examples.explanation: First 1's next greater is 2; 2 has none; Second 1's next greater is 2 (circular).

entries.title: Online Stock Span
entries.problemStatement:
Design an algorithm that collects daily price quotes for some stock and returns the span of that stock's price for the current day.

The span of the stock's price in one day is the maximum number of consecutive days (starting from that day and going backward) for which the stock price was less than or equal to the price of that day.

For example, if the prices of the stock in the last four days is [7,2,1,2] and the price of the stock today is 2, then the span of today is 4 because starting from today, the price of the stock was less than or equal 2 for 4 consecutive days.

Implement the StockSpanner class:
- StockSpanner() Initializes the object.
- int next(int price) Returns the span of the stock's price given that today's price is price.
entries.description: Calculate stock price span using monotonic stack
constraints: At most 10^4 calls will be made to next.

entries.title: 132 Pattern
entries.problemStatement:
Given an array of n integers nums, a 132 pattern is a subsequence of three integers nums[i], nums[j] and nums[k] such that i < j < k and nums[i] < nums[k] < nums[j].

Return true if there is a 132 pattern in nums, otherwise, return false.
entries.description: Find if there exists a 132 pattern in array

examples.explanation: No 132 pattern exists.
There is a 132 pattern: [1, 4, 2].
There are three 132 patterns: [-1, 3, 2], [-1, 3, 0] and [-1, 2, 0].

entries.title: Maximum Frequency Stack
entries.problemStatement:
Design a stack-like data structure to push elements to the stack and pop the most frequent element from the stack.

Implement the FreqStack class:
- FreqStack() constructs an empty frequency stack.
- void push(int val) pushes an integer val onto the top of the stack.
- int pop() removes and returns the most frequent element in the stack. If there is a tie, the element closest to the top is removed and returned.
entries.description: Design a stack that pops the most frequent element

examples.output: [null, null, null, null, null, null, null, 5, 7, 5, 4]
examples.explanation: After pushes, frequencies are 5:3, 7:2, 4:1. Pop returns 5 (most frequent), then 7, 5, 4.

constraints: At most 2 * 10^4 calls will be made to push and pop.

entries.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
entries.problemStatement:
You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a given stock on the ith day.

You want to maximize your profit by choosing a single day to buy one stock and choosing a different day in the future to sell that stock.

Return the maximum profit you can achieve from this transaction. If you cannot achieve any profit, return 0.
entries.description: Find the maximum profit from buying and selling a stock

examples.explanation: Buy on day 2 (price = 1) and sell on day 5 (price = 6), profit = 6-1 = 5.

You are given an array of integers nums, and there is a sliding window of size k which is moving from the very left of the array to the very right. You can only see the k numbers in the window. Each time the sliding window moves right by one position.

Return the max sliding window - an array of the maximum values in each window.
entries.description: Find maximum in each sliding window of size k.

entries.title: Minimum Window Substring
entries.problemStatement:
Given two strings s and t of lengths m and n respectively, return the minimum window substring of s such that every character in t (including duplicates) is included in the window. If there is no such substring, return the empty string "".

The testcases will be generated such that the answer is unique.

s does not contain two a's, so return empty string.

constraints: s and t consist of uppercase and lowercase English letters.

entries.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
entries.problemStatement: You are given a string s and an integer k. You can choose any character of the string and change it to any other uppercase English character. You can perform this operation at most k times. Return the length of the longest substring containing the same letter you can get after performing the above operations.
entries.description: Find longest substring with same letter after k replacements

examples.explanation: Replace the two A's with two B's or vice versa.
Replace one A in the middle to get "AABBBBA" or similar.

entries.title: LRU Cache

- int get(int key) Return the value of the key if the key exists, otherwise return -1.
- void put(int key, int value) Update the value of the key if the key exists. Otherwise, add the key-value pair to the cache. If the number of keys exceeds the capacity from this operation, evict the least recently used key.

The functions get and put must each run in O(1) average time complexity.

Example, with capacity 2:

```
LRUCache(2)
put(1, 1)     cache holds 1
put(2, 2)     cache holds 1, 2
get(1)   -> 1 reading 1 counts as using it
put(3, 3)     over capacity, so 2 is evicted
get(2)   -> -1
put(4, 4)     over capacity, so 1 is evicted
get(1)   -> -1
get(3)   -> 3
get(4)   -> 4
```

3. Read in next the characters until the next non-digit character or the end of the input is reached. The rest of the string is ignored.
4. Convert these digits into an integer (i.e. "123" -> 123, "0032" -> 32). If no digits were read, then the integer is 0. Change the sign as necessary (from step 2).
5. If the integer is out of the 32-bit signed integer range [-2^31, 2^31 - 1], then clamp the integer so that it remains in the range. Specifically, integers less than -2^31 should be clamped to -2^31, and integers greater than 2^31 - 1 should be clamped to 2^31 - 1.
6. Return the integer as the final result.

entries.description: Replace words in a sentence with their shortest root from a dictionary

examples.input: dictionary = ["cat","bat","rat"], sentence = "the cattle was rattled by the battery"
examples.output: "the cat was rat by the bat"
examples.explanation: "cattle" -> "cat", "rattled" -> "rat", "battery" -> "bat"
Each word is replaced by its shortest root.

constraints: dictionary[i] consists of only lower-case letters.
sentence consists of only lower-case letters and spaces.
The number of words in sentence is in the range [1, 1000]
The length of each word in sentence is in the range [1, 1000]
Every two consecutive words in sentence will be separated by exactly one space.
sentence does not have leading or trailing spaces.

entries.title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
entries.problemStatement:
Design a data structure that supports adding new words and finding if a string matches any previously added string.

Implement the WordDictionary class:
- WordDictionary() Initializes the object.
- void addWord(word) Adds word to the data structure, it can be matched later.
- bool search(word) Returns true if there is any string in the data structure that matches word or false otherwise. word may contain dots '.' where dots can be matched with any letter.
entries.description: Design a data structure that supports adding words and searching with wildcards

examples.explanation: addWord adds words, search("pad") returns false (not added), search(".ad") matches "bad","dad","mad"

constraints: word in addWord consists of lowercase English letters.
word in search consists of "." or lowercase English letters.
At most 10^4 calls to addWord and search.

entries.title: Single Number
entries.problemStatement:
Given a non-empty array of integers nums, every element appears twice except for one. Find that single one.

You must implement a solution with a linear runtime complexity and use only constant extra space.
entries.description: Find the element that appears only once in an array where every other element appears twice
constraints: Each element in the array appears twice except for one element which appears only once.

entries.title: Number of 1 Bits
entries.problemStatement: Write a function that takes the binary representation of an unsigned integer and returns the number of '1' bits it has (also known as the Hamming weight).
entries.description: Count the number of set bits (1s) in a binary representation

examples.explanation: The input binary string has three '1' bits.
The input binary string has one '1' bit.
The input binary string has thirty one '1' bits.

constraints: The input must be a binary string of length 32

entries.title: Counting Bits
entries.problemStatement: Given an integer n, return an array ans of length n + 1 such that for each i (0 <= i <= n), ans[i] is the number of 1's in the binary representation of i.
entries.description: Return an array where ans[i] is the number of 1s in the binary representation of i

entries.title: Reverse Bits
entries.problemStatement:
Reverse bits of a given 32 bits unsigned integer.

Note:
- Note that in some languages, such as Java, there is no unsigned integer type. In this case, both input and output will be given as a signed integer type.
- The input will be given as a binary string of length 32.
entries.description: Reverse bits of a given 32-bit unsigned integer

examples.explanation: The input binary string represents the unsigned integer 43261596, so return 964176192 whose binary representation is 00111001011110000010100101000000.

constraints: The input must be a binary string of length 32

entries.title: Missing Number
entries.problemStatement: Given an array nums containing n distinct numbers in the range [0, n], return the only number in the range that is missing from the array.
entries.description: Find the missing number in an array containing n distinct numbers from 0 to n

examples.explanation: n = 3 since there are 3 numbers, so all numbers are in the range [0,3]. 2 is the missing number.
n = 2 since there are 2 numbers, so all numbers are in the range [0,2]. 2 is the missing number.

constraints: All the numbers of nums are unique.

entries.title: Sum of Two Integers
entries.problemStatement: Given two integers a and b, return the sum of the two integers without using the operators + and -.
entries.description: Calculate the sum of two integers without using + or - operators

entries.title: Jump Game
entries.problemStatement:
You are given an integer array nums. You are initially positioned at the array's first index, and each element in the array represents your maximum jump length at that position.

Return true if you can reach the last index, or false otherwise.
entries.description: Determine if you can reach the last index of an array by jumping

examples.explanation: Jump 1 step from index 0 to 1, then 3 steps to the last index.
You will always arrive at index 3 no matter what. Its maximum jump length is 0, which makes it impossible to reach the last index.

entries.title: Jump Game II
entries.problemStatement:
You are given a 0-indexed array of integers nums of length n. You are initially positioned at nums[0].

Each element nums[i] represents the maximum length of a forward jump from index i. In other words, if you are at nums[i], you can jump to any nums[i + j] where:
- 0 <= j <= nums[i] and
- i + j < n

Return the minimum number of jumps to reach nums[n - 1]. The test cases are generated such that you can reach nums[n - 1].
entries.description: Find minimum number of jumps to reach the last index

examples.explanation: The minimum number of jumps to reach the last index is 2. Jump 1 step from index 0 to 1, then 3 steps to the last index.

constraints: It's guaranteed that you can reach nums[n - 1].

entries.title: Gas Station
entries.problemStatement:
There are n gas stations along a circular route, where the amount of gas at the ith station is gas[i].

You have a car with an unlimited gas tank and it costs cost[i] of gas to travel from the ith station to its next (i + 1)th station. You begin the journey with an empty tank at one of the gas stations.

Given two integer arrays gas and cost, return the starting gas station's index if you can travel around the circuit once in the clockwise direction, otherwise return -1. If there exists a solution, it is guaranteed to be unique.
entries.description: Find the starting gas station to complete a circular tour

examples.explanation: Start at station 3 (index 3) and fill up with 4 unit of gas. Tank = 4. Travel to station 4 (cost 1). Tank = 3. Fill up (5 gas). Tank = 8. Travel to station 0 (cost 2). Tank = 6. And so on...
You can't start at any station as you don't have enough gas to reach the next station.

entries.title: Task Scheduler
entries.problemStatement:
Given a characters array tasks, representing the tasks a CPU needs to do, where each letter represents a different task. Tasks could be done in any order. Each task is done in one unit of time. For each unit of time, the CPU could complete either one task or just be idle.

However, there is a non-negative integer n that represents the cooldown period between two same tasks (the same letter in the array), that is that there must be at least n units of time between any two same tasks.

Return the least number of units of times that the CPU will take to finish all the given tasks.
entries.description: Find minimum intervals needed to execute all tasks with cooldown

examples.explanation: A -> B -> idle -> A -> B -> idle -> A -> B. There is at least 2 units of time between any two same tasks.
On this case any permutation of size 6 would work since n = 0.

constraints: The integer n is in the range [0, 100].

entries.title: Partition Labels
entries.problemStatement:
You are given a string s. We want to partition the string into as many parts as possible so that each letter appears in at most one part.

Note that the partition is done so that after concatenating all the parts in order, the resultant string should be s.

Return a list of integers representing the size of these parts.
entries.description: Partition a string into maximum parts where each letter appears in at most one part

examples.explanation: The partition is "ababcbaca", "defegde", "hijhklij". This is a partition so that each letter appears in at most one part.
All characters share the same partition.

constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

entries.title: Hand of Straights
entries.problemStatement:
Alice has some number of cards and she wants to rearrange the cards into groups so that each group is of size groupSize, and consists of groupSize consecutive cards.

Given an integer array hand where hand[i] is the value written on the ith card and an integer groupSize, return true if she can rearrange the cards, or false otherwise.
entries.description: Determine if cards can be rearranged into groups of consecutive cards

examples.explanation: Alice's hand can be rearranged as [1,2,3],[2,3,4],[6,7,8]
Alice's hand cannot be rearranged into groups of 4.

entries.title: Valid Parenthesis String
entries.problemStatement:
Given a string s containing only three types of characters: '(', ')' and '*', return true if s is valid.

The following rules define a valid string:
- Any left parenthesis '(' must have a corresponding right parenthesis ')'.
- Any right parenthesis ')' must have a corresponding left parenthesis '('.
- Left parenthesis '(' must go before the corresponding right parenthesis ')'.
- '*' could be treated as a single right parenthesis ')' or a single left parenthesis '(' or an empty string "".
entries.description: Check if a string with wildcards can be a valid parentheses string

examples.explanation: The * can be treated as (

entries.title: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
entries.problemStatement:
A triplet is an array of three integers. You are given a 2D integer array triplets, where triplets[i] = [ai, bi, ci] describes the ith triplet. You are also given an integer array target = [x, y, z] that describes the triplet you want to obtain.

To obtain target, you may apply the following operation on triplets any number of times (possibly zero):
- Choose two indices (0-indexed) i and j (i != j) and update triplets[j] to become [max(ai, aj), max(bi, bj), max(ci, cj)].

Return true if it is possible to obtain the target triplet [x, y, z] as an element of triplets, or false otherwise.
entries.description: Check if target triplet can be formed by taking max of triplet components

examples.explanation: Merge triplets [2,5,3] and [1,7,5] to get [2,7,5].
It is impossible to obtain [3,2,5] since 2 is not in any triplet.

entries.title: Maximum Units on a Truck
entries.problemStatement:
You are assigned to put some amount of boxes onto one truck. You are given a 2D array boxTypes, where boxTypes[i] = [numberOfBoxesi, numberOfUnitsPerBoxi]:
- numberOfBoxesi is the number of boxes of type i.
- numberOfUnitsPerBoxi is the number of units in each box of type i.

You are also given an integer truckSize, which is the maximum number of boxes that can be put on the truck. You can choose any boxes to put on the truck as long as the number of boxes does not exceed truckSize.

Return the maximum total number of units that can be put on the truck.
entries.description: Find maximum number of units that can be put on a truck with limited capacity

examples.explanation: Take 1 box of type 0 (3 units) + 2 boxes of type 1 (2*2=4 units) + 1 box of type 2 (1 unit) = 8 units total
Sort by units per box descending, then greedily take boxes
